title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is reworking the combinatorial description of (possibly folded, non-oriented) maps by a finite set of 'repères' (flags) acted on by involutions. On the previous page he notes that index 1 played a special role because rho_1^2 = 1. To remove this asymmetry he introduces the free product of three groups of order 2, Pi^tau_03 = <tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf | tau_i^2 = 1>, with no relation (tau_0 tau_inf)^2 = 1. He also introduces its index-2 subgroup of even words, Pi_03 = <rho_0, rho_1, rho_inf | rho_inf rho_1 rho_0 = 1>, which is free of rank 2, i.e. pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}).

(14) The identification is rho_inf = tau_1 tau_0, rho_1 = tau_0 tau_inf, rho_0 = tau_inf tau_1. Indeed rho_inf rho_1 rho_0 = tau_1 tau_0 tau_0 tau_inf tau_inf tau_1 = 1.

(15) Hence G_2 ≅ Pi^tau_03 / <<rho_1^2>> and G_2^0 ≅ Pi_03 / <<rho_1^2>>. Here G_2 is the (non-oriented) cartographic group <s0, s1, s2 | s_i^2 = (s0 s2)^2 = 1>, and G_2^0 is its oriented index-2 subgroup, isomorphic to Z * Z/2. The normal closures of rho_1^2 in Pi^tau_03 and in Pi_03 agree, because conjugation by any tau_i sends rho_1 to rho_1^{-1}.

Interpretation: Pi^tau_03 is the 'classifying' group for 'weighted triangular maps'. These are triangulated surfaces (X, K) with a labelling of the vertices S -> {0, 1, inf} such that every triangle has exactly one vertex of each label, i.e. a proper 3-colouring of the triangulation. The 'repères' (weighted flags) are now the triangles. tau_i is the reflection of a triangle across its side opposite the vertex of type i; the no-boundary hypothesis means the tau_i act without fixed points. Around each vertex the triangles alternate, so vertex orders are even. The 'reduced order' (order/2) is the ramification index, i.e. the order of the corresponding rho_i in the local monodromy.

In modern terms: finite sets with three fixed-point-free involutions correspond to (possibly non-orientable) hypermaps, i.e. 3-coloured triangulations. Equivalently these are the real-structure picture of dessins d'enfants: the preimage under a Belyi map of the decomposition of P^1(C) into upper and lower half-planes. The even subgroup Pi_03 recovers the oriented dessins / transitive Pi_03-sets. Ordinary maps are the special case rho_1^2 = 1, i.e. reduced order 2 at type-1 vertices, which gives the quotient G_2. The next page states the resulting equivalence (17): finite triangulated maps ≃ finite Pi^tau_03-sets with fixed-point-free involutions. It then begins the oriented version, defined via a subset R^+ of the flags.
errors: The parenthetical '(qui est une subd. barycentrique!)' is accurate only when type-1 vertices have reduced order 2 (rho_1^2 = 1, ordinary maps). A general 3-coloured triangulation is the 'barycentric subdivision' of a hypermap, not of a cell decomposition of the surface. This is a minor imprecision or loose wording.
Notation '<rho_1^2>' must be read as normal closure. Harmless, and the closures coincide in Pi^tau_03 and Pi_03.

ideas.what: Free product of three Z/2 (with an index-2 even subgroup that is free of rank 2) as the symmetric replacement for the cartographic group; the cartographic group as the quotient by rho_1^2
ideas.modern_name: Extended triangle group Delta*(inf,inf,inf) / free product Z/2*Z/2*Z/2; cartographic groups C_2, C_2^+
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978), Bryant–Singerman (1985), Jones and collaborators on hypermaps; Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984) for the cartographic group terminology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on cartographic groups and dessins

ideas.what: Weighted triangular maps: 3-coloured triangulations whose flags are triangles, with tau_i the reflection across the side opposite vertex i; vertex order even, reduced order = half
ideas.modern_name: Hypermaps (Walsh/Cori bipartite-map picture), non-orientable hypermaps, real structure of dessins d'enfants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cori (1975), Walsh (1975), Jones–Singerman; Malgoire–Voisin (Montpellier, 1977) for cellular maps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions triangulations coming from Belyi maps / the barycentric picture; the explicit 3-involution version is not clearly there

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard reformulation, the hypermap / extended triangle group description of dessins, written out by Grothendieck for himself. It is consistent with the Esquisse and with the Jones–Singerman literature. Nothing here is absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: The group in (15) and in the following sentence is written Pi^tau_03 (pi with superscript tau, as in (12) on the previous page), not a tilde: (15) G_2 ≃ Pi^tau_03/<rho_1^2>, G_2^0 ≃ Pi_03/<rho_1^2>; 'Ici Pi^tau_03 apparaît comme le groupe classifiant'.
The angle brackets in (15) denote the normal subgroup generated by rho_1^2.
On the next page, 'Pi_03^C' and the operators 'pi_i' are probably Pi^tau_03 and tau_i respectively.
